scope: Remove standalone Core owner prevalidation only; retain final owner validation and both receipt lookups

lock_analysis.Core: Existing Core._state_lock remains held continuously over recovery.validate_task_success -> owner.commit_output_publication -> recovery.commit_validated_transition.
lock_analysis.Recovery: RecoveryManager owns no separate lock; validate_task_success copies TaskRecord twice, mutates only after copy, then reads lineage. commit_validated_transition remains assignment-only under caller composition lock.
lock_analysis.Owner: Public commit_output_publication unchanged: exact plan deep rebuild, owner lock acquisition, final state/attempt/collection/manifest validation, detached receipt+edges+locations allocation, then owner mutation. Its lock is not widened around recovery.
lock_analysis.why: No prior validation result is reused as authority. The retained owner commit is still the final validation boundary; recovery plan is discarded if owner fails.
lock_analysis.unsafe_alternative: Removing final owner validation or carrying a prepared token across lock release would require revision coverage across publication, current attempt, collection, retirement and fences, or a new continuously locked API. That alternative was not needed or implemented.
lock_analysis.counterexample_to_unchecked_token: After a hypothetical owner preflight and before commit, another owner transition may start collection/retirement or advance attempt; a stale unchecked token would overwrite the new state. Existing final commit rejects this. Same-thread RLock reentrancy also prevents a lock-owned flag alone from proving revision stability.

concrete_operations.ordinary: refs=False sends one real INLINE envelope through Core owner/recovery adoption, retains Complete and runs GC on exact replay.
concrete_operations.contained: refs=True uses two exact contained transfers already prepared/promoted by the real local journal/child owners; failures must leave both child states unchanged and later successful replay releases pins on GC.
faults: Recovery validate_task_success returns a candidate success plan, live recovery/owner checked unchanged, then raises: owner commit and recovery commit forbidden.

After successful recovery preflight, mutate detached owner plan descriptor with same-length different bytes. Existing public owner commit must reject checksum before owner writes; recovery commit forbidden. Original envelope unchanged and replay succeeds.

tests.existing_fault_preserved: Old helper still calls actual owner preflight then throws, but injection moved to commit entry so removal cannot silently skip the negative case.
tests.registration: All five whole-file selectors are already registered. Hash refresh required only if trial evaluated; no registry changed here.

cost.removed_work: One public owner validate call, one deep plan/envelope/manifest rebuild+digest path and one owner state validation before every first owner CAS. Actual Python internal replace recursion may rebuild nested values multiple times, so no fabricated exact hash-count speedup.
cost.unchanged_cost: Two preexisting receipt queries and final commit validation remain; no copy/detachment is removed at public boundary.
cost.test_delta: Two imports and one 4-case function; existing failure hook adapted.
cost.assessment: Favorable minimal candidate; needs requested existing bounded tests before acceptance. Larger revision/token optimization is not justified by this case.
